## Purpose

Advance the install-wide `morning-daily` schedule by one step: reserve today's
zoned morning report once its planned instant has passed, build or recover its
evidence snapshot, and finalize any report whose author deadline expired with its
deterministic fallback. Repeated ticks are safe; each one only moves rows forward.

## When a playbook uses it

The report service or a system playbook calls it on a short cadence (the reviewed
minute-tick playbook is the next implementation slice). Project and worker
principals are refused: the schedule is install-wide, not per project.

## How it works internally

`src/commands/report_commands.py` refuses any principal other than a service or an
unscoped system playbook, validates `reports` config, and reads `now` (default:
wall clock). With `reports.morning.enabled` off it cancels every pending row and
returns `state: disabled`.

Otherwise `src/reports/schedule.py` resolves today's planned instant in
`reports.timezone` (a nonexistent DST minute moves to the first real minute, a
repeated one takes its first occurrence) and the next due instant.
`reserve_morning_report` in `src/database/queries/morning_report_queries.py` takes
an advisory lock and inserts one `morning-<local date>` row per day, snapshotting
the config, window, previous default-branch heads and 72-hour fact membership. A
zone edit cannot reserve within 20 hours of the last reservation
(`timezone_guard`), and a tick after `late_cutoff_minutes` records
`skipped:late_start`.

Each `building` or `failed` row is claimed under a 300-second lease, collected with
`collect_morning_evidence` from its stored window and context, and stored `ready`
with a `src/reports/fallback.py` report (32 KiB cap, omissions counted). A row
whose author deadline has passed is finalized; terminal rows older than 90 days
are pruned.

## Side effects and persistence

Writes `morning_reports`, `morning_report_facts` and `morning_report_coverage`
(`src/database/tables.py`, revision `a00000000030`). Coverage cursors and heads
advance only on finalization and only for sources that read successfully; failed
sources stay anchored at the window start for recovery. Ready briefs and their
hashes are never rebuilt. Every step is durable, so a daemon restart resumes from
the stored rows.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`out_of_scope` means the caller is not the report service or an unscoped system
playbook. `report.invalid` reports a config validation error or a non-finite
`now`. A collection failure does not fail the tick: the row moves to
`failed:snapshot_unavailable` and the next tick retries it. `state: waiting` with
`reason` `before_schedule`, `timezone_guard` or `covered` means nothing was due.
Inspect stored rows with `aq report list` and `aq report show ID`.
